LESSON: NUMBER SEQUENCING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Numbers 2.3 Counting Concrete Objects (10 lessons) By the end of the Sub Strand,
Topic 2.4: Number Sequencing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Number Sequencing, part of Numbers 2.3 Counting Concrete Objects (10 lessons) By the end of the Sub Strand, in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do number come after one another?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Randomly pick number cut outs/number cards in turns from a pile and identify the number. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive devices to perform given tasks, while those with speech difficulties could use other alternative modes of communication to share their responses.

2. Arrange numbers in sequence.

3. Work with others in purposive groups/pairs to complete missing numbers in sequence by placing the appropriate number cards or cut outs,

4. Sing/hum/clap/tap songs on number sequence with peers as they mention their family members,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Randomly pick number cut outs/number cards in turns from a pile and identify the number. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive devices to perform given tasks, while those with speech difficulties could use other alternative modes of communication to share their responses.
2. Arrange numbers in sequence.
3. Work with others in purposive groups/pairs to complete missing numbers in sequence by placing the appropriate number cards or cut outs,
4. Sing/hum/clap/tap songs on number sequence with peers as they mention their family members,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Number Sequencing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: learners arrange numbers in sequence and complete number puzzles.

Values:
Peace: learners harmoniously sing songs on number sequence 1-9 together.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Hygiene: learners observe hygiene as they sequence number cards; not put cards in the mouth because they may be dirty.

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able to relate singing songs on number sequence to singing games in Creative Activities.
